Payment Gateway Architecture Overview

This document describes the architecture of the Meridian Financial Services (MFS) Payment Gateway v2, covering the modernized payment processing stack.

System Architecture

The payment gateway is deployed on OpenShift in the mfs-prod namespace with the following topology:

  • mfs-pay-pod-01 - Primary payment processing pod (active)
  • mfs-pay-pod-02 - Secondary payment processing pod (active)
  • mfs-pay-pod-03 - Tertiary payment processing pod (standby/overflow)
  • mfs-vault-pod-01 - Token vault and HSM integration pod
  • mfs-settle-pod-01 - Settlement batch processing pod

Service Accounts

AccountPurposeScope
svc-payment-apiPayment gateway API authentication and authorizationmfs-prod, mfs-staging
svc-token-vaultHSM key retrieval and token vault operationsmfs-prod
svc-settlementSettlement batch processing and file generationmfs-prod
svc-notification-svcAlert and notification deliverymfs-prod

Database Architecture

Primary database: mfs_payments_db (PostgreSQL 15) on pghost-prod-01.mfs.internal

Key schemas and tables:

  • card_tokens - Tokenized cardholder data
  • token_audit_log - Token operation audit trail
  • cardholder_data - Encrypted cardholder records (AES-256-GCM)
  • retry_ledger - Idempotent retry state tracking
  • currency_rates - FX rate cache
  • conversion_audit - Currency conversion audit trail
  • settlement_batches - Settlement batch metadata
  • settlement_records - Individual settlement records
  • gateway_ledger - Payment gateway transaction ledger

Audit database: mfs_audit_db (PostgreSQL 15) on pghost-prod-01.mfs.internal

API Endpoints

Base URL: https://api.mfs.internal/payment/v2

  • POST /tokens - Create payment token
  • GET /tokens/{id} - Retrieve token metadata
  • POST /payments - Process payment
  • POST /payments/{id}/retry - Retry failed payment
  • GET /payments/{id}/status - Payment status
  • POST /settlements/batch - Trigger settlement batch
  • GET /settlements/{batchId} - Settlement batch status

Related Resources

  • PCI DSS Compliance Checklist
  • Settlement Engine Design
  • Payment API Reference
  • Incident Runbook: Payment Timeouts

Settlement Engine Technical Design

Technical design document for the real-time settlement processing engine (Epic EPC-103, Feature PAY-300).

Overview

The settlement engine replaces the legacy T+1 batch settlement system with near-real-time processing capability. It runs on mfs-settle-pod-01 in the mfs-prod OpenShift namespace using the svc-settlement service account.

Settlement Batch Processing (PAY-301)

State Machine

PENDING -> AGGREGATING -> GENERATING -> SUBMITTED -> CONFIRMED
                                                       |
                                                   FAILED (retry)

Sequence Flow

  1. Batch trigger received (scheduled or on-demand via API)
  2. BatchAggregator groups transactions from gateway_ledger table in mfs_payments_db
  3. Transactions grouped by: merchant_id, currency, acquiring_bank
  4. ISO 8583 settlement file generated per acquirer
  5. Files transmitted to acquirer SFTP endpoints
  6. Settlement confirmation received and recorded in settlement_records table

Performance Targets

  • 100K transactions per batch within 5-minute SLA
  • Parallel aggregation with configurable thread pool (default: 8 threads)
  • Database batch inserts with 1000-record chunks

Balance Reconciliation (PAY-302)

Reconciliation Flow

  1. Listen for settlement batch completion events on Kafka topic mfs.settlement.completed
  2. Load gateway ledger entries for the batch period from mfs_payments_db
  3. Load settlement confirmation records
  4. Match gateway entries against settlement confirmations
  5. Flag discrepancies exceeding $0.01 threshold
  6. Write results to mfs_audit_db reconciliation tables
  7. Send alerts via svc-notification-svc for unresolved discrepancies

Database Schema

All tables in mfs_payments_db on pghost-prod-01.mfs.internal:

  • settlement_batches - Batch metadata (id, status, created_at, completed_at, transaction_count)
  • settlement_records - Per-transaction settlement records linked to batch
  • reconciliation_results - Reconciliation outcomes per batch (in mfs_audit_db)

Payment Gateway API v2 Reference

API reference for the MFS Payment Gateway v2. Base URL: https://api.mfs.internal/payment/v2

Authentication: Bearer token via svc-payment-api service account OAuth2 client credentials flow.

Tokenization Endpoints

POST /api/v2/tokens

Create a payment token from cardholder data.

Request:
{
  "pan": "4111111111111111",
  "expiry_month": 12,
  "expiry_year": 2028,
  "cardholder_name": "John Doe"
}

Response (201):
{
  "token_id": "tok_mfs_abc123def456",
  "last_four": "1111",
  "brand": "visa",
  "created_at": "2026-09-20T10:00:00Z"
}

GET /api/v2/tokens/{token_id}

Retrieve token metadata (never returns raw PAN).

Payment Endpoints

POST /api/v2/payments

Process a payment using a token.

Request:
{
  "token_id": "tok_mfs_abc123def456",
  "amount": 99.99,
  "currency": "USD",
  "merchant_id": "merch_001",
  "idempotency_key": "pay_20260920_001"
}

Response (201):
{
  "payment_id": "pay_mfs_xyz789",
  "status": "completed",
  "amount": 99.99,
  "currency": "USD"
}

POST /api/v2/payments/{payment_id}/retry

Retry a failed payment with idempotency guarantee.

GET /api/v2/payments/{payment_id}/status

Check payment processing status.

Currency Endpoints

GET /api/v2/currencies/rates

Get current exchange rates for supported currencies (USD, EUR, GBP, JPY, CAD, AUD, CHF).

POST /api/v2/payments/convert

Process a payment with currency conversion.

Request:
{
  "token_id": "tok_mfs_abc123def456",
  "amount": 100.00,
  "source_currency": "EUR",
  "target_currency": "USD",
  "merchant_id": "merch_002"
}

Settlement Endpoints

POST /api/v2/settlements/batch

Trigger a settlement batch. Requires svc-settlement service account.

GET /api/v2/settlements/{batch_id}

Get settlement batch status and summary.

Error Codes

CodeDescription
PAY-001Invalid token
PAY-002Insufficient funds
PAY-003Currency not supported
PAY-004Duplicate idempotency key
PAY-005Circuit breaker open
PAY-006Settlement batch in progress

Incident Runbook: Payment Gateway Timeouts

Runbook for diagnosing and resolving payment processing timeout incidents on the MFS Payment Gateway.

Last incident: INC0080101 (2026-09-28) - Payment timeout spike on mfs-pay-pod-01

1. Initial Triage

  1. Check Grafana dashboard Payment Gateway SLOs for p99 latency spike
  2. Check Datadog monitor Payment API Latency P99 for alert status
  3. Identify affected pods: oc get pods -n mfs-prod -l app=mfs-payment-gateway
  4. Check pod health: oc describe pod mfs-pay-pod-01 -n mfs-prod

2. Database Connection Investigation

  1. Check active connections to mfs_payments_db on pghost-prod-01.mfs.internal:
    SELECT count(*) FROM pg_stat_activity WHERE datname = 'mfs_payments_db';
  2. Check for long-running queries:
    SELECT pid, now() - pg_stat_activity.query_start AS duration, query FROM pg_stat_activity WHERE datname = 'mfs_payments_db' AND state != 'idle' ORDER BY duration DESC;
  3. Check connection pool metrics via Prometheus (exported by svc-payment-api):
    hikari_connections_active{pod=~"mfs-pay-pod-.*"}

3. Connection Pool Tuning

Lesson from INC0080101: After the tokenization deployment (CHG0090101), connection pool exhaustion occurred due to longer-running tokenization queries.

  • Default pool size: 20 connections per pod
  • Recommended: 50 connections per pod for tokenization workload
  • Query timeout: 3 seconds (added post-INC0080101)

To update pool config:

oc edit configmap mfs-payment-gateway-config -n mfs-prod
# Update:
#   spring.datasource.hikari.maximum-pool-size: 50
#   spring.datasource.hikari.connection-timeout: 3000
oc rollout restart deployment/mfs-payment-gateway -n mfs-prod

4. Token Vault Latency

If timeout is related to token operations (check svc-token-vault metrics):

  1. Check HSM session pool on mfs-vault-pod-01
  2. Verify PKCS#11 session count: should be 20 (increased from 5 after INC0080102 investigation)
  3. Check Datadog monitor Token Vault Response Time

5. Circuit Breaker Status

If retry handler circuit breaker is open:

  1. Check circuit breaker state: GET /actuator/circuitbreakers on affected pod
  2. Review recent failure pattern in retry_ledger table
  3. Circuit breaker auto-recovers via half-open probe every 30 seconds

6. Escalation

  • L1: DevOps & SRE (Li Wei, Raj Patel)
  • L2: Platform Engineering (Sarah Chen, David Okoye)
  • L3: Payment Services (Marcus Rivera, Alex Kim)
